 "architecture": "Both bots are single-function priority cascades, not utility planners or formal state machines; a mode label is only a debug string.\n\nOwn TS bot: per tick: (1) bookkeeping from events and sounds (who damaged us, drone attackers, long-range laser hits, pickup memory, kill count); (2) free-for-all detector; (3) upgrade pick from a fixed ranked list; (4) target choice by a lowest-score rule; (5) retreat flag with hysteresis; (6) fire control per weapon; (7) movement in two branches. With a target: base strafe at a weapon-dependent range, then a chain of overrides where the later one wins: path toward target if no line of sight; cover point if retreating; go fetch a second weapon if gun-only, target beyond 90 m and unhurt for 3 s; break line of sight after a long-range laser hit; \"peek spot\"; dodge a charging laser; blend toward zone if unsafe. Without a target: zone, then supply drop, then weapon pickup, then cubes, then (flag off) crates, then drone farming, then home spot (free-for-all only) or a zone goal. Then a quiet-walk speed cap, a wall nudge, stuck escape, and idle aim. Two experiment switches exist: \"regen\" on, \"grow\" (wider farming) off.\n\nShipped Python engine: fixed mode order: zone-urgent > cover (when retreating, or \"many\" threats, or outranged, or hiding) unless a \"close fight\" exception applies > zone must-go > hold > cube > loot (when holding neither laser nor lightning) > fight > loot > roam. Behaviour variants are toggled by a comma-separated environment flag set; defaults are quiet walking and fast strafe flips; \"patient\", \"early\" and \"laser_tight\" exist but are off. It carries per-tick wall-clock guards (skips far line-of-sight checks after 15 ms, stops A* work at 26 ms, cover search bails at 28-33 ms).",
 "navigation": "Own TS bot: 2 m grid. A cell is blocked if a prism spans the band from 1.2 m to 9.5 m above local ground, if terrain slope exceeds 48 degrees, or at the map border. A two-pass distance transform gives clearance in cells (all eight neighbours cost one, so diagonal clearance is overstated). A* is 8-connected, requires clearance of at least 2 cells (4 m), forbids corner cutting, adds a wall-hugging penalty (large at clearance 2, small at 3), is capped at 40,000 expansions and returns the best partial route. Start and goal snap to the nearest free cell by ring search. Following: go straight if the goal is under 60 m and the line is walkable; otherwise replan when the goal moved more than 8 m, every 4 s, or after drifting more than 12 m; steer at the farthest of the next 25 waypoints reachable in a straight walkable line. A final nudge rotates the move by up to about 2.2 rad if the point 5 m ahead is too close to a wall. Stuck rule: under 1.2 m of displacement in about a second while commanding movement triggers a 1.2 s escape (first half: random roughly perpendicular direction with a jump; second half: jump plus jet forward). No roof use at all: pickups and cubes more than 3 m above ground are skipped unless already within 6 m. Body size is fixed (does not grow with cubes). The path search and sight checks are warmed up 12 times at start-up to pre-heat the JIT.\n\nShipped Python engine: 2 m raster storing one lowest-base and one highest-top per cell (scanline polygon fill), nearest-sample terrain. Walk grid at 4 m; a cell is free if its centre and four points 2.5 m around are unblocked. A* is incremental across ticks (time-sliced, 25,000-node cap, 2 s cooldown after failure, reused while the goal stays within 4 cells). Following looks ahead up to 32 m of route for the farthest clear waypoint and replans if more than 28 m off route. Local steering scores 16 headings by alignment with the goal plus a little inertia, minus penalties for being blocked at 3, 6 and 10 m. No path planning in fight mode or when more than 3 m above ground. Stuck rule: ground speed below 2.5 m/s for 0.6 s while pushing; if the obstacle ahead is less than 40 m tall and energy is above 35 it jump-jets over it for 2.5 s, otherwise a random 90-plus-degree detour for 1.5 s. A separate progress watchdog every 2.5 s (goal more than 20 m away but under 5 m moved) forces a replan and, on the second strike, a climb. It also jump-jets onto roofs for a wanted pickup once within 14 m horizontally.",
 "aiming_and_fire_control": "Own TS bot. Gun: three-pass linear intercept using the gun's projectile speed, aimed at the body centre (4.5 m, scaled by the target's cubes; 1.75 m for drones), with half of the vertical velocity applied. Fires when yaw error is inside the angle subtended by about 2.2 m at that range (floor 0.012 rad), pitch 1.3 times looser, range under 95% of maximum, magazine not reloading. Reload only when no mech is targeted, not firing, and the magazine is under half. Laser: starts charging as soon as it is off cooldown and the target is visible; keeps holding until about 97% charge AND aligned AND visible, then releases; lets go just before the forced auto-fire; keeps holding while the target is briefly hidden. Lightning: fires when visible, inside 97% of range, yaw within 24 degrees of the target, and energy above the shot cost plus 6 (plus 30 when farming). Mortar: used only against mechs at 28-220 m; closed-form ballistic angle with three lead iterations, low arc with line of sight and high arc without; takes over the torso when the gun is reloading or blocked; fires within 0.025 rad on both axes; never while a laser charge is in progress. Idle aim: face the last damage bearing for 2.5 s, else a heard sound for 1.5 s, else sweep about +/-75 degrees around the travel direction.\n\nShipped Python engine. Gun lead is two passes with an extra 0.05 s latency term and vertical lead clamped to +/-6 m. The laser gets its own aim (current position plus 0.1 s of velocity) but the torso only switches to it once the charge is full; before that it tracks the gun solution. Tolerances are loose: yaw within the angle of 1.6 body radii, pitch within 3 m. If the laser is about to auto-fire and is not aligned it releases anyway. Lightning fires only within 12 degrees of aim (the rulebook allows 30) and energy above cost plus 1. Reload when idle below 60% magazine. If damaged by an attacker it cannot see, it stops shooting the current target (unless that target is within 45 m or a laser charge is running) and turns toward the damage bearing.\n\nShared target-selection ideas. TS: score = distance + 0.12 x enemy HP, minus 40 if shootable, minus 60 for the current target (stickiness), minus 120 if \"killable now\", minus 20 if it is aiming at us. \"Killable now\" is a magazine-aware burst estimate: rounds left (max 9) x damage x a measured hit rate by range (0.8 under 50 m, 0.6 under 100 m, 0.35 beyond), plus a full laser shot if it is within 0.8 s of ready, plus up to 8 lightning ticks limited by energy, all scaled by the cube damage bonus. Python: distance + 0.2 x HP, minus 100 below 30% HP, minus 120 stickiness, minus 40 if it hit us in the last 4 s, plus 400 if not shootable.",
 "survival_and_anti_squad_tactics": "Own TS bot. (1) Retreat with hysteresis: start when HP fraction drops below 0.40 plus 0.15 per extra enemy that is aiming at us with line of sight (cap 0.75); stop above 0.85. Retreat is cancelled if the target is in sight and either has less than half our HP or is killable by the current burst. While retreating out of sight it holds fire so the 5 s regeneration timer can start. (2) Cover point: 16 directions x radii 6-55 m; candidate must be walkable with 6 m clearance, zone-safe, and hidden from the threat's eye at both waist and head height; prefers far from the threat and close to us; cached 1 s; boosts to it. (3) \"Peek spot\" for multi-hunter fights: within 30 m, a spot with a line of fire to the chosen target that none of up to four other visible hostiles (within 200 m) can see; used only if it hides us from all of them; recomputed every 0.5 s. (4) Long-range laser response: if a laser hits us from a mech more than 60 m away (or unseen) and we hold no laser, break its line of sight for 3 s using cover within 30 m. (5) Laser dodge: an enemy charging with its aim on us ducks us behind cover within 12 m with boost. (6) Gun-only against a laser holder: close to 30 m with boost instead of trading at 70 m. (7) Preferred ranges: 70 m gun, 26 m with lightning and energy above 25, 95 m with laser, 85 m with mortar; strafe direction re-randomised every 0.8-2.4 s. (8) Quiet walking below the footstep threshold when nothing is urgent. (9) Heals to 85% before farming drones or crates.\n\nShipped Python engine. Goes to cover when HP is under 38% (until 80%, or 60% after 12 quiet seconds), when 3+ threats are visible, 2+ with HP under 60%, incoming damage above 110 per second over 2.5 s, any unseen attacker, or when outranged (an enemy laser beyond 70 m and no laser of our own). Exceptions: it keeps fighting at under 40 m if it has lightning or HP above 50%, and when \"finishing\" (target under 30% HP within 130 m, own HP above 30%, at most 2 threats). Cover search: 16 directions x 7-75 m along walkable rays, minimising the count of the three nearest threat eyes that can see the spot, biased away from them; if no fully hidden spot exists it either goes for a weapon within 90 m, stands and trades, or (if outranged, healthy, one threat) charges to 22 m. Unseen attackers become a pseudo-threat placed 120 m along the damage bearing so cover is computed against them. Projectile dodging: sidestep off a charging laser's aim line when within about 7 m of it (consistent side per enemy, skipped inside 40 m if we hold lightning because lightning cancels the charge); sidestep bullets predicted to pass within 3.8 m in the next 0.45 s; forward-simulate mortar shells to their landing point and run directly away if it is within 13 m and under 3.5 s. Fight ranges 110 m laser / 28 m lightning / 85 m gun, 55 or 28 m when finishing. The \"jink\" flag flips strafe side every 0.35-0.9 s.\n\nNothing in either bot models the squad explicitly (no hunter counting over time, no early-solo-hunter plan, no late-game plan). The team's own conclusion is that every caution-type change they submitted lowered the practice score.",
 "loot_weapons_upgrades": "Weapon preference. TS: laser first, lightning a close second, mortar far behind, gun last; a pickup must clearly beat the current second weapon. Remembers every pickup it has seen and forgets one when it is within 25 m and no longer listed. Search radius 260 m when gun-only, 130 m otherwise; boosts to a first extra weapon. Python: wants only laser and lightning, never a mortar (a laser hit on a mortar holder does +60%); drops the gun first once it finds both; search 240 m if it has neither, 160 m otherwise; remembers pickups and crates.\n\nUpgrades (both, fixed order, survival first): plating, armor, nanites, then laser damage, lightning efficiency, gun damage/rate, laser charge, then gyros, lightning range, gun magazine, capacitor, reactor, servos, sensors, gun velocity, jets, and mortar items last. Not conditioned on which weapons are held.\n\nCubes: TS collects visible ground cubes within 90 m only when no mech is targeted. Python collects within 70 m mid-fight if HP is above 35%, at most one threat, and the cube is within 10 m or the target is beyond 60 m; 120 m when roaming.\n\nCrates: TS shoots crates within 55 m only when idle and above 85% HP. Python shoots crates within 150 m, stands about 22 m off, and walks to remembered crates up to 260 m away when above 60% HP with no threats.\n\nDrones: TS shoots drones within 70 m when healthy, always shoots one that hit it in the last 4 s (out to 100 m), approaches to 25 m with lightning or 40 m otherwise; in free-for-all mode only in self-defence. Python farms drones within 140 m when above 55% HP, standing about 50 m off.\n\nSupply drops: TS goes if within 220 m, it can arrive about when it lands, the spot is zone-safe and nobody else holds it; boosts beyond 30 m; stands still inside half the ring radius; only considered when no mech is targeted. Python: within 170 m, no threats, HP above 45%, skips if someone else has more than 1.5 s of capture progress.",
 "zone_and_endgame": "TS: a point is \"zone-safe\" if it is inside the zone as it will be 3 s from now with a 10-15 m margin, and the next circle can be reached in time (walking at about 10 m/s plus a 12 s buffer). When unsafe with no target it paths to a goal on its own side of the next circle (at most 45% of the next radius from the centre, i.e. it does not run to the middle); in a fight it blends 40% fight movement with the zone direction and boosts only when actually outside. In free-for-all mode the destination is a \"home\" spot: 90 random samples inside 85% of the next circle, cost = precomputed exposure, travel distance, crowding (mechs seen in the last 20 s within 80 m, supply drops within 60 m, drones within 50 m) and a penalty for being nearer the centre than 75% of the radius, re-picked every 4 s with hysteresis.\n\nPython: margin = min(30 m, 30% of next radius); \"must go\" when walking time plus 12 s exceeds the time left (24 s with the off-by-default \"early\" flag); \"urgent\" when outside or within 8 m of the current edge. Zone travel heads straight for the next centre, and idle roaming drifts in until within 55% of the next radius. Dodging is halved when the zone is urgent.\n\nNeither bot has endgame-specific logic (no final-circle positioning, no handling of the zero-radius last circle, no late change in aggression apart from the Python \"patient\" rule that always engages when four or fewer are alive, which is off).",
 "housebot_observations": "From their report and tools (their claims, not re-measured by me):\n- Practice squad: house bots share vision, never fight each other, send one hunter early, more as you kill them, all of them late. Practice points are therefore roughly \"house bots we kill before we die\"; hiding does not score.\n- Practice replays the same 48 seeds every time: identical code gives an identical score (another team reported 4.44 twice). Any code change reshuffles outcomes chaotically, so swings of about +/-0.4 between versions are noise-level.\n- Submission limit: 4 per rolling hour. The version that plays the final is the chosen submission (best practice score unless another is picked on the track page before the cutoff).\n- Qualifying is 16 matches and the final 64 matches of real free-for-all; Expert house bots fill empty seats there and are strong (one averaged about 4.2th place and held about 17 cubes).\n- A house-bot type named after another team's design (\"probe-astra-finalist\") killed their bot in 16 of 39 private-room deaths.\n- Recorded mechs (house and human) stand still only about 9% of the time, boost 20-30% of the time, and jet a lot in fights.\n- Private rooms on the public play server fill empty seats with house bots but play as a free-for-all, so they do NOT reproduce the practice squad format; the spectator feed of a room is a full replay in the same format as the official sample replay.\n- Rulebook facts they rely on: a mech moving at or below 5 m/s on the ground makes no footstep sound (steps carry 40 m, boost 90 m); lightning hits within 30 degrees of aim yaw and cancels a laser charge for 2 s.",

 "novel_ideas": [
  "Two modes in one bot, switched by a cheap invariant: in practice the house squad never kills its own, so if more mechs are dead than we have killed (plus one for zone or drone deaths) the match must be a free-for-all; then switch from hunting to hiding. Useful for a build that must score in practice and also survive the final.",
  "Magazine-aware finishing: estimate the damage we can deliver in the next couple of seconds from rounds left, range-dependent hit rate, laser readiness and energy for lightning, and strongly prefer (and refuse to retreat from) a visible target whose HP is below that number.",
  "Peek spot: when several hostiles are around, fight from a nearby point that has a line of fire to the one chosen target but is hidden from every other visible hostile; otherwise stay put.",
  "Retreat threshold that rises with the number of enemies currently aiming at us, with a wide hysteresis band, and holding fire while hidden so the 5 s regeneration timer is not reset by our own shots.",
  "Quiet walking just under the 5 m/s footstep threshold whenever nothing is urgent, so hunters lose sound cues; exempt zone travel, first-weapon runs, drops and the seconds after taking damage.",
  "Treat a long-range laser hit specifically: with no laser of our own, break line of sight for about one laser cycle rather than trading; when gun-only against a laser holder, close to about 30 m instead of duelling at 70 m.",
  "Unseen attacker handling: place a phantom threat about 120 m along the damage bearing so cover and facing react before the attacker is visible.",
  "Projectile-aware dodging: forward-simulate mortar shells to their landing point and step away; sidestep bullets on a predicted near pass; keep a consistent dodge side per charging laser; do not dodge a nearby laser if holding lightning, because lightning cancels the charge.",
  "Danger-weighted waiting spot for free-for-all: prefer the outer ring (about 75% of the next radius) and low crowding over low exposure, because their data says crowding and centrality predict death and exposure does not.",
  "Offline precomputed exposure map shipped as a small binary (4 m cells, fraction of sampled ground positions within 160 m that can see a mech there, canopy modelled as blocking after a few metres).",
  "Testing on the real engine via private rooms on the public play server with full spectator replays, plus small analysis scripts for accuracy by weapon, damage taken by attacker and weapon, time standing/boosting/airborne, stuck spots, and the last 15 s before death. Caveat: rooms are free-for-all, not the squad format.",
  "Because practice seeds are fixed and outcomes are chaotic under any code change, they treat differences under about 0.4 as noise; a useful prior when judging our own A/B results.",
  "Stuck recovery by jump-jetting over the obstacle when it is low enough and energy allows, with a second slower watchdog for jitter in a pocket; time-sliced path search with wall-clock guards so a slow language never misses the 50 ms deadline."
 ],

  "TS bot: the laser is released using the gun's lead solution, so against a strafing target at long range the hitscan beam is aimed ahead of the target; there is no separate no-lead laser aim.",
  "TS bot: sight checks use a 2.5D height field sampled every 1.5 m that ignores tree trunks and canopy at run time and treats any prism starting near the ground as solid up to its top, so overhangs and bridges are wrong; the Python engine merges all prisms in a cell into one base-to-top interval with the same effect.",
  "TS bot: later movement overrides replace strafing with a straight walk to a peek or cover point that is recomputed every 0.5-1 s, which invites oscillation and predictable movement under fire; the peek override also wins over the laser line-of-sight break.",
  "No roof or jet use in the TS bot beyond stuck escape; elevated pickups and cubes are skipped. Body radius is fixed, so clearance is wrong after collecting cubes.",
  "Reload only happens when no mech is targeted; there is no tactical reload behind cover with a nearly empty magazine.",
